# select_team_member (Resource)

One member of a team: a user, identified by email address, or an SSO group, identified by its name. Use one of these per member, for example with `for_each` over a list of email addresses.

## About

Each `select_team_member` adds one user or one SSO group to one team. Use `for_each` over a set of email addresses to manage many members; adding or removing an email then changes only that member. Members that Terraform does not manage are not changed.

A user is identified by email address and an SSO group by its name as your identity provider reports it. The provider does not create users: they sign in through your identity provider.

This resource is backed by SELECT's v2 API, at `/v2/teams/{team_id}/members`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "select_team" "data_engineering" {
  name = "Data Engineering"
}

# One select_team_member per user, so adding or removing an email changes only
# that member.
locals {
  data_engineers = toset([
    "alice@example.com",
    "bob@example.com",
  ])
}

resource "select_team_member" "data_engineers" {
  for_each = local.data_engineers

  team_id    = select_team.data_engineering.id
  type       = "user"
  identifier = each.value
}

# A team lead with the admin role on the team.
resource "select_team_member" "lead" {
  team_id    = select_team.data_engineering.id
  type       = "user"
  identifier = "carol@example.com"
  role       = "admin"
}

# Everyone in an SSO group from your identity provider.
resource "select_team_member" "platform_group" {
  team_id    = select_team.data_engineering.id
  type       = "sso_group"
  identifier = "platform-engineers"
  role       = "viewer"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `identifier` (String) The user's email address, or the SSO group's name as the identity provider reports it. Changing it forces a new member.
- `team_id` (String) The team to add the member to. Changing it removes the member from the old team and adds it to the new one.
- `type` (String) Whether the member is an individual user (`user`) or an SSO group (`sso_group`). Changing it forces a new member.

### Optional

- `role` (String) The member's role within the team: `admin`, `editor` or `viewer`. Defaults to `editor`. Changes in place.

### Read-Only

- `create_time` (String) When the member was added to the team — RFC 3339 UTC.
- `etag` (String) Opaque strong ETag for this membership. Sent as `If-Match` on updates and deletes so a change made outside Terraform cannot be silently overwritten.
- `id` (String) The membership's identifier in SELECT, assigned when the member is added. Use it with `terraform import`, as `team_id/id`, to bring an existing member under management.

## Import

`select_team_member` can be imported using the team ID and the member ID, separated by a forward slash:

```bash
terraform import select_team_member.example <team_id>/<member_id>
```

To find the member ID, list the team's members with the API:

```bash
curl -s https://api.select.dev/v2/teams/$TEAM_ID/members \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SELECT_API_KEY" \
  -H "x-tenant-id: $SELECT_ORGANIZATION_ID" | jq '.items[] | {id, type, identifier, role}'
```

## Additional Information

### Only `role` changes in place

A change to `role` is an update. A change to `team_id`, `type` or `identifier` removes the member and adds a new one.

### How the provider reads a member

The API has no route that returns one member, so the provider lists the team's members and finds this one by its ID. If the member is not in the list, for example because someone removed it in the SELECT UI, the next plan adds it again.

### The all-users team

The built-in all-users team includes every organization member automatically. The API always lists no members for it, so this resource cannot read back a member of that team, and every plan would add the member again. Do not use the all-users team as `team_id`.

### Changes made outside Terraform

Every write carries the member's `etag` as an `If-Match` header, so an update or delete is refused if the member changed since Terraform last read it. When that happens, run `terraform apply -refresh-only` to pick up the current state and then apply again.
